title:
SCALA: Semi-supervised Cascade for Left Atrial Scar,
Cavity, and Multi-Structure CT Segmentation
abstract:
Segmenting left atrial structures remains challenging on both magnetic resonance imaging and
computed tomography: atrial scar is small and wall-adherent, LGE-MRI intensity carries no
absolute scale, acquisition varies between centers, and thin pulmonary veins dominate
boundary-based metrics. We
introduce \emph{SCALA}, a semi-supervised cascade for the three tasks of the MICCAI 2026 CARE
LeftAtrium challenge, covering atrial scar quantification on LGE-MRI, left atrial cavity
segmentation, and multi-structure cardiac CT segmentation. Three task-specific residual-encoder
nnU-Net models share one training recipe and one deployment pipeline but no parameters, and are
never trained jointly. For scar, an out-of-fold cavity prediction supplies anatomical
localization and two derived channels, an intensity ratio normalized by the blood pool and a
signed distance to the endocardial surface. We exploit the nested annotation structure through
self-training and ensemble complementary members, then convert probability into the reported
metric with structure-specific decision rules, an on-wall component filter for scar and a
double-threshold vein hysteresis for CT. A residual acquisition-grid mismatch is corrected by
sub-slice offset voting fixed by the spacing ratio.
Cross-validation gives surface scar Dice $0.722$, cavity Dice $0.925$ and CT mean Dice $0.961$,
while the hidden test sets return generalized Dice (\gdsc) $0.363$ for scar and Dice $0.830$ and
$0.954$ for cavity and CT.

\keywords{Left atrial segmentation \and Atrial scar quantification
\and \mbox{LGE-MRI} \and Semi-supervised learning \and nnU-Net}
